question: Why is our auto business shrinking this year?

grade.reason: Nothing to find: needs the LLM grader (Phase 3).

report.interpretation: I read "shrinking" as a fall in the size of the auto book. I measured it with auto policies in force and earned premium by month, from Jan 2025 to Sep 2026, and compared Jan–Sep 2026 with Jan–Sep 2025. I also checked auto claim counts by loss quarter.
report.answer: The data doesn't show the auto business shrinking this year. Auto policies in force rose from about 29,712 in Jan 2025 to 30,075 in Jan 2026 and 30,269 in Sep 2026. Earned premium for Jan–Sep 2026 was $22.54M, against $22.30M for Jan–Sep 2025, about 1.1% higher. Every region grew slightly (California, North, Southeast, Texas). The business is growing slowly, by roughly 1% a year. Auto claim counts by loss quarter were 713, 721, 652 and 634 in 2025, then 644, 643 and 750 in 2026. They are not falling this year, and Q3 2026 is the highest of the seven quarters even though recent weeks are still incomplete because of late reporting. If you saw a decline somewhere, it may be a different measure or a narrower slice. Examples are a single state, channel or cause, claim counts by report date, or the most recent incomplete weeks. Tell me which and I'll look into it.
report.answer_sql: SELECT month, sum(policies_in_force) AS policies_in_force, sum(earned_premium) AS earned_premium FROM exposure_monthly WHERE product='auto' AND month>='2025-01-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

findings.claim: Auto policies in force and earned premium are flat to slightly rising, not shrinking. Jan–Sep 2026 earned premium is about 1.1% above Jan–Sep 2025.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT round(sum(CASE WHEN month>='2026-01-01' THEN earned_premium END)) ep_2026_jan_sep, round(sum(CASE WHEN month<'2025-10-01' THEN earned_premium END)) ep_2025_jan_sep FROM exposure_monthly WHERE product='auto'

data_quality_issues.issue: The latest weeks' claims are incomplete because claims are reported late.
data_quality_issues.impact: Recent claim counts may be understated. This doesn't affect the exposure and premium figures. The exposure table has no duplicates or empty values.

tool_calls.sql:
WITH source AS (
    SELECT * FROM exposure_monthly
)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', month) AS DATE) AS period, sum(policies_in_force) / count(DISTINCT month) AS value
FROM source
WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND month <= DATE '2026-09-30'
  AND product IN ('auto')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL

WITH source AS (
    SELECT * FROM exposure_monthly
)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', month) AS DATE) AS period, sum(earned_premium) AS value
FROM source
WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND month <= DATE '2026-09-30'
  AND product IN ('auto')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL

WITH source AS (
    SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
           c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
    FROM claims c
    JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id
    ) pay USING (claim_id)
)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('quarter', loss_date) AS DATE) AS period, count(*) AS value
FROM source
WHERE loss_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND loss_date <= DATE '2026-09-30'
  AND product IN ('auto')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL
